meanings: (Tw) to interview (e.g. for a report or feature story)

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 访 relates to visiting someone to speak with them or ask questions.
方 (fāng) gives a sound distantly related to fǎng, having drifted apart over time.
口 (mouth) — 问 relates to speaking, specifically asking a question.
门 (mén) gives a hint of the sound — 问 is pronounced wèn, related but the tone and vowel have shifted.

example.hanzi: 科学家们访问了南极的科考站。
example.pinyin: kēxuéjiāmen fǎngwèn le Nánjí de kēkǎozhàn.
example.english: The scientists visited the research station in Antarctica.
example.fact: Antarctica's McMurdo Station, the continent's largest research base, houses around 1,000 people in summer but fewer than 200 through the dark winter months — its buildings sit on volcanic rock near Mount Erebus, one of the few permanently active volcanoes on Earth.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 设's meaning 'to establish, set up,' something first proposed through words.
殳 (shū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shè.
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'

example.hanzi: 探险队设法穿过了茂密的雨林。
example.pinyin: tànxiǎnduì shèfǎ chuānguò le màomì de yǔlín.
example.english: The expedition team found a way to cross the dense rainforest.
example.fact: The Amazon rainforest produces roughly 20% of the world's oxygen and is home to an estimated 10% of all known species on Earth. Satellite monitoring shows it has lost about 17% of its original forest cover since 1970 to logging and agriculture.

meanings: interjection of wonder, shock or admiration

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哎 is a sound made with the mouth, an interjection.
艾 (ài) gives a sound close to āi, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.
口 (mouth) — 呀, a spoken particle, comes from the mouth.
牙 (yá) gives the sound — an exact match with 呀.

example.hanzi: 哎呀,火山突然喷发了!
example.pinyin: āiyā, huǒshān tūrán pēnfā le!
example.english: Oh no, the volcano suddenly erupted!
example.fact: When Krakatoa erupted in 1883, the explosion was so loud it ruptured eardrums of sailors 40 miles away and was heard clearly nearly 3,000 miles away in Australia — one of the loudest sounds ever recorded in human history.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 慷 describes an inner quality, generosity of spirit.
康 (kāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 慷's reading.
忄 (heart) — 慨 describes emotion felt in the heart, a sigh.
既 (jì) gives a sound distantly related to 慨's reading kǎi, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 那位商人慷慨地捐赠了一座图书馆。
example.pinyin: nà wèi shāngrén kāngkǎi de juānzèng le yí zuò túshūguǎn.
example.english: That merchant generously donated a library.
example.fact: Andrew Carnegie gave away roughly 90% of his fortune during his lifetime, funding over 2,500 public libraries around the world. It remains a philanthropic model still studied today for spreading free access to knowledge across small towns.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 迷 originally described losing one's way while walking, extending to 'confused, obsessed.'
米 (mǐ) gives a sound distantly related to mí, having drifted apart over time.
丿 (something falling) — an object slipping away.
夫 (a hand/person) — the object slipping out of a hand, giving 失 its meaning 'to lose.'

example.hanzi: 登山者在浓雾中迷失了方向。
example.pinyin: dēngshānzhě zài nóngwù zhōng míshī le fāngxiàng.
example.english: The climber lost his sense of direction in the thick fog.
example.fact: Magnetic north drifts constantly — it has moved over 600 miles across the Arctic since 1900 and is currently migrating toward Siberia at roughly 30 miles per year, forcing periodic updates to navigation charts and compass calibrations worldwide.

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 细 relates to something as fine and thin as silk thread
田 (tián) gives a loose sound connection to 细's reading xì
⺼ (flesh/body) — 胞 relates to the body, originally the womb.
包 (bāo) is an exact match for the sound of 胞.

example.hanzi: 显微镜下可以看到细胞的结构。
example.pinyin: xiǎnwéijìng xià kěyǐ kàndào xìbāo de jiégòu.
example.english: Under the microscope you can see the structure of the cell.
example.fact: The human body contains an estimated 37 trillion cells, and red blood cells alone are replaced at a rate of about 2 million per second. That means nearly the entire population of red blood cells turns over roughly every four months.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 验 originally related to examining or testing horses, later extended to 'to test, examine, verify'
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound connection to 验's reading yàn
尸 is traditionally read as a picture of a person collapsed or bent over — the origin of its meaning 'corpse.'

example.hanzi: 法医对尸体进行了验尸。
example.pinyin: fǎyī duì shītǐ jìnxíng le yànshī.
example.english: The forensic examiner performed an autopsy on the body.
example.fact: The word "autopsy" comes from the Greek "autopsia," meaning "to see for oneself." The practice dates back to ancient Alexandria, where physicians such as Herophilus conducted systematic human dissections around 300 BC to study anatomy.

components.note: 母 (mǔ, 'mother') serves as the phonetic base; the sound has since diverged from měi, so the connection is mostly historical today.
日 (sun) — the sun is what disappears as evening falls
免 (to escape, avoid) — pictured as the sun slipping away, giving 晚 its sense of 'late, evening'

example.hanzi: 他每晚都在阳台上看星星。
example.pinyin: tā měiwǎn dōu zài yángtái shàng kàn xīngxīng.
example.english: Every night he watches the stars from the balcony.
example.fact: Light pollution now hides the Milky Way from more than a third of humanity, including nearly 80% of North Americans. That's a remarkably recent change — as late as the 1950s, most of the world's population could still see it clearly from their backyard.

components.note: 开 (open, here representing a frame or opening) — 形 pictures light passing through a gap.
彡 (streaks or rays of light) — light and pattern coming through an opening gave 形 its meaning 'shape' or 'form.'

戊 (a halberd, a type of ancient weapon) was the original core of this character, and 成 pictured the completion of forging or assembling that weapon. Over time the meaning broadened from this specific craft image to the general sense of 'to complete' or 'to become.' The reading chéng has stayed fairly close to its ancient pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 长期的风化作用形成了这片沙漠。
example.pinyin: chángqī de fēnghuà zuòyòng xíngchéng le zhè piàn shāmò.
example.english: Long-term weathering formed this desert.
example.fact: The Sahara has actually flipped between desert and lush grassland roughly every 20,000 years due to shifts in Earth's axial tilt, a cycle called the "green Sahara" period. The most recent green phase ended only about 5,000 years ago.

components.note: Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

临 is traditionally read as a person bending down to look, drawn above a cluster of objects arranged below. The image shows someone looking down over many things spread beneath them, the source of 临's core meaning 'to face, to overlook, to arrive at.' The sense of 'befalling' or 'approaching,' as in 来临 'to arrive,' grew naturally from this picture of arriving to look upon a scene.

example.hanzi: 冬天的来临让北极熊开始寻找食物。
example.pinyin: dōngtiān de láilín ràng běijíxióng kāishǐ xúnzhǎo shíwù.
example.english: The arrival of winter prompts polar bears to start searching for food.
example.fact: Polar bears can smell a seal's breathing hole through nearly three feet of compacted snow and ice. Their stomachs can stretch to hold up to 150 pounds of food after a successful hunt, critical for surviving months of sparse hunting.

components.note: Depicts a child wrapped in swaddling, related to 子 (child); the picture-meaning has nothing to do with its modern grammatical role marking a completed action or change of state.
纟 (thread) — 结 relates to tying or knotting threads together.
吉 (jí) gives a hint of the sound — 结 is pronounced jié, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 双方终于了结了这场官司。
example.pinyin: shuāngfāng zhōngyú liǎojié le zhè chǎng guānsi.
example.english: Both sides finally settled the lawsuit.
example.fact: The Peace of Westphalia in 1648, which finally settled the Thirty Years' War, involved simultaneous negotiations at two German cities, Münster and Osnabrück, because the warring Catholic and Protestant delegates refused to meet under the same roof. It remains one of the earliest examples of modern multilateral diplomacy.

components.note: 彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.

业 (simplified from 業) originally pictured the jagged, notched top edge of a large wooden frame used to hang bells or chime-stones in ancient ritual orchestras. Because such instrument racks represented significant craftsmanship and achievement, the meaning extended over time to 'occupation, trade, undertaking,' and later 'achievement.'

example.hanzi: 人工智能正在改变许多行业。
example.pinyin: réngōng zhìnéng zhèngzài gǎibiàn xǔduō hángyè.
example.english: Artificial intelligence is transforming many industries.
example.fact: The global semiconductor industry produces over a trillion chips a year, yet more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips are manufactured by a single company, TSMC, in Taiwan. That concentration makes the industry unusually vulnerable to regional disruption.

meanings: abbr. for Union of Soviet Socialist Republics

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — 苏 relates to certain aromatic plants and to reviving, coming back to life
稣 (sū) gives the sound — 苏 is also pronounced sū, an exact match
耳 (ear) — 联 originally meant 'connected, linked,' perhaps through the image of joined loops.
关 (guān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lián.

example.hanzi: 1991年苏联解体了。
example.pinyin: 1991 nián Sūlián jiětǐ le.
example.english: The Soviet Union dissolved in 1991.
example.fact: At its peak the Soviet Union spanned 11 time zones and covered roughly one-sixth of Earth's land surface. After its 1991 collapse, it split into fifteen independent countries, the largest peaceful dissolution of a state in modern history.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 潜 describes hiding beneath the surface of water.
替 (tì) gives a sound distantly related to qián, having drifted apart over time.
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 这个年轻球员展现出巨大的潜力。
example.pinyin: zhège niánqīng qiúyuán zhǎnxiàn chū jùdà de qiánlì.
example.english: This young player has shown enormous potential.
example.fact: The human brain uses about 20% of the body's total energy despite making up just 2% of body weight. The popular myth that people use "only 10% of their brain," however, is false — imaging shows nearly all brain regions are active over a typical day.

components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'
辶 (to walk) — encountering someone often happens while moving or traveling.
禺 (yú) gives a sound close to yù, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 小说描写了一段复杂的外遇。
example.pinyin: xiǎoshuō miáoxiě le yí duàn fùzá de wàiyù.
example.english: The novel depicts a complicated affair.
example.fact: Emperor penguins are famously monogamous for a single breeding season but re-pair with a different partner nearly every year. Studies tracking banded birds found fewer than 15% of pairs reunite for a second season, despite the species' reputation for devotion.

components.note: 氵 (water) — sand forms as water erodes rock over time.
少 (shǎo) shares the initial sh- with shā, though the vowel has since shifted.
扌 (hand) — relates directly to 拉's meaning 'to pull, drag,' an action done by hand.
立 (lì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted noticeably from lā.

example.hanzi: 她午餐只吃了一份沙拉。
example.pinyin: tā wǔcān zhǐ chī le yí fèn shālā.
example.english: She only ate a salad for lunch.
example.fact: The Caesar salad wasn't invented in Rome or by a chef named Caesar. It was created in 1924 by Italian-American restaurateur Caesar Cardini in Tijuana, Mexico, reportedly improvised from limited ingredients during a busy Fourth of July weekend.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) suggests following a path.
尊 (to honor) shows respect for what is being followed, giving 遵 its meaning 'to obey, to comply with.'
令 (an order, command) — 命 pictures issuing a command.
口 (mouth) — a command given aloud gave 命 its meaning 'order' or 'decree,' and by extension, 'fate' or 'life.'

example.hanzi: 士兵回答道:"遵命,长官!"
example.pinyin: shìbīng huídá dào: "zūnmìng, zhǎngguān!"
example.english: The soldier replied, "Yes sir, as ordered!"
example.fact: The rigid chain-of-command culture in military organizations traces back to Prussian army reforms of the early 1800s. Those reforms formalized standardized ranks, drills, and staff systems that most modern militaries, including NATO forces, still structurally resemble today.

components.note: 丶 (a dot) — represents the burning flame atop a lamp.
王 here depicts the base and stand of an oil lamp, not its usual meaning 'king' — the one who tends the flame became linked to 'master, lord, main.'
扌 (hand) — relates directly to 持's meaning 'to hold, maintain.'
寺 (sì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from chí.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 她是一名很受欢迎的电视节目主持人。
example.pinyin: tā shì yì míng hěn shòu huānyíng de diànshì jiémù zhǔchírén.
example.english: She is a very popular TV show host.
example.fact: Johnny Carson hosted NBC's "The Tonight Show" for nearly 30 years, from 1962 to 1992, and at his peak commanded roughly 17 million viewers a night. No single late-night host has matched that scale of nightly reach since television fragmented across cable and streaming.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 举 relates to lifting or raising something with the hand
舉 (jǔ) is the traditional character's own form, giving the sound directly, an exact match
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.

example.hanzi: 他的这个举动让所有人感到惊讶。
example.pinyin: tā de zhège jǔdòng ràng suǒyǒu rén gǎndào jīngyà.
example.english: This action of his surprised everyone.
example.fact: Jane Goodall's 1960s observations of chimpanzees using grass stems to fish termites out of mounds were among the first documented cases of tool use by non-human animals. The discovery forced scientists to redefine what separates humans from other species.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 倒 relates to a person falling over
到 (dào) gives the sound — 倒 is also pronounced dào, an exact match
攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 数 relates to the action of counting.
娄 (lóu) gives a hint of the sound — 数 is pronounced shù, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 人群一起倒数迎接新年。
example.pinyin: rénqún yìqǐ dàoshǔ yíngjiē xīnnián.
example.english: The crowd counted down together to welcome the new year.
example.fact: NASA's launch countdown tradition is partly credited to the 1929 German science-fiction film "Frau im Mond" (Woman in the Moon). Its director, Fritz Lang, added the countdown purely for dramatic suspense, and the convention stuck for real rocket launches decades later.

meanings: abbr. for 費拉德爾菲亞|费拉德尔菲亚[Fei4 la1 de2 er3 fei1 ya4]

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — 费 relates to spending money, fees, and expenses
弗 (fú) gives a loose sound connection to 费's reading fèi
土 (earth) — relates to 城's meaning 'city, wall,' since city walls were built of earth.
成 (chéng) gives the sound — 城 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 独立宣言是在费城签署的。
example.pinyin: Dúlì Xuānyán shì zài Fèichéng qiānshǔ de.
example.english: The Declaration of Independence was signed in Philadelphia.
example.fact: Philadelphia's Liberty Bell, a symbol of American independence, has been cracked since at least 1846. The flaw reportedly worsened during a test ring for George Washington's birthday, and the bell has not been rung since for fear of causing further damage.

components.note: 手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
至 (zhì, to arrive) — carries 到's core meaning, 'to reach, to arrive'
刂 (a form of 刀, dāo) gives a sound close to 到's pronunciation dào

example.hanzi: 雾太大了,我们看不到山顶。
example.pinyin: wù tài dà le, wǒmen kànbudào shāndǐng.
example.english: The fog is too thick; we can't see the mountain peak.
example.fact: Mount Everest's summit is shrouded in cloud or storm for most of the year. Climbers have only a narrow weather window, usually in May, when jet-stream winds temporarily shift and expose the peak long enough for a safe summit attempt.

meanings: various birds of the family Columbidae

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — 鸽 names a type of bird, the pigeon or dove.
合 (gě) gives a sound close to gē, the same syllable with a different tone.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 广场上有很多鸽子。
example.pinyin: guǎngchǎng shàng yǒu hěn duō gēzi.
example.english: There are many pigeons in the square.
example.fact: Homing pigeons carried messages across enemy lines in both World Wars. One bird named Cher Ami saved nearly 200 American soldiers in 1918 by delivering a critical message despite being shot through the breast and losing a leg during the flight.

components.note: 又 (hand) shows a hand performing an action.
戈 (spear) — mock combat and stage tricks with weapons gave 戏 its meaning 'play, drama.'
刂 (knife) contributes to the character's form, though its link to 剧's meaning 'drama' has faded over time.
居 (jū) gives a rhyme close to jù, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 这部戏剧改编自莎士比亚的作品。
example.pinyin: zhè bù xìjù gǎibiān zì Shāshìbǐyà de zuòpǐn.
example.english: This drama is adapted from a work by Shakespeare.
example.fact: Shakespeare's Globe Theatre in London could hold roughly 3,000 spectators, many of them "groundlings" who paid just a penny to stand in the open-air yard. The original building burned down in 1613 after a stage cannon set the thatched roof alight.

components.note: 少 depicts a few small dots or grains, like scattered sand — a simple picture of a small quantity, giving the meaning 'few' or 'little.'
女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.

example.hanzi: 那位少女梦想成为一名科学家。
example.pinyin: nà wèi shàonǚ mèngxiǎng chéngwéi yì míng kēxuéjiā.
example.english: That young girl dreams of becoming a scientist.
example.fact: Marie Curie became the first person ever to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences — physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911. She conducted much of her early radioactivity research in a converted shed with no proper ventilation, unaware of the health risks.

components.note: 尤 (particularly/outstanding) — relates to 就's sense of approaching or arriving at a particular point
京 (jīng, capital) gives a sound close to 就's pronunciation jiù
⺮ (bamboo) — the material of ancient counting rods.
具 (held in two hands) — bamboo counting rods or an abacus held up for use, the tools of calculation that gave 算 its meaning 'to calculate, count.'

example.hanzi: 就算下雨,比赛也会照常进行。
example.pinyin: jiùsuàn xiàyǔ, bǐsài yě huì zhàocháng jìnxíng.
example.english: Even if it rains, the match will go on as scheduled.
example.fact: Wimbledon didn't install a retractable roof over Centre Court until 2009, after decades of rain delays. The tournament's grass courts are reseeded and closely monitored every year, since natural turf reacts unpredictably to even brief periods of wet weather.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'

example.hanzi: 一支小队负责搜救失踪的登山者。
example.pinyin: yì zhī xiǎoduì fùzé sōujiù shīzōng de dēngshānzhě.
example.english: A small team was responsible for rescuing the missing climber.
example.fact: Mountain rescue dogs can search an area the size of several football fields in about 30 minutes, a task that could take a human search team hours. Their sense of smell is estimated to be tens of thousands of times more sensitive than a human's.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — a hand gripping something tightly
丸 (a pebble/pellet) — the small object held firmly in the hand
灬 (fire) — relates to 照's meaning 'to shine, illuminate; photograph.'
昭 (zhāo) gives a sound hint — 照 is pronounced zhào, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他刚拿到驾驶执照。
example.pinyin: tā gāng nádào jiàshǐ zhízhào.
example.english: He just got his driver's license.
example.fact: The world's first driving license law was introduced in France in 1893, requiring drivers to pass a technical exam and pledge not to endanger pedestrians. That came decades before most countries required any test at all to legally operate a motor vehicle.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.
钅 (metal) — 镖 names a small metal throwing weapon, a dart.
票 (piào) gives a sound close to biāo, sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 那位明星有三名保镖跟随。
example.pinyin: nà wèi míngxīng yǒu sān míng bǎobiāo gēnsuí.
example.english: That celebrity is followed by three bodyguards.
example.fact: The U.S. Secret Service originally had nothing to do with presidential protection — it was founded in 1865 primarily to fight the widespread counterfeiting of currency. It only began guarding presidents full-time after President McKinley's assassination in 1901.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 热 relates directly to heat
执 (zhí) gives a loose sound connection to 热's reading rè
纟 (thread) — relates directly to 线's meaning 'line, thread, wire.'
戋 (jiān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from xiàn.

example.hanzi: 请拨打客服热线咨询问题。
example.pinyin: qǐng bōdǎ kèfú rèxiàn zīxún wèntí.
example.english: Please call the customer service hotline with any questions.
example.fact: The "red telephone" hotline between Washington and Moscow, established in 1963 after the Cuban Missile Crisis, was never actually a phone at first. It was a teletype machine, chosen because typed messages left an unambiguous record to prevent dangerous mistranslation during a crisis.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — fighting back with bare hands
亢 — the throat, a vulnerable point defended while resisting
讠 (speech) — relates to 议's meaning 'to discuss, deliberate; opinion.'
义 (yì) gives the sound — 议 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 数千人走上街头抗议新法案。
example.pinyin: shùqiān rén zǒushàng jiētóu kàngyì xīn fǎ'àn.
example.english: Thousands of people took to the streets to protest the new bill.
example.fact: The 1773 Boston Tea Party, one of history's most famous protests, saw colonists dump an estimated 92,000 pounds of tea into Boston Harbor. Its cleanup value in today's currency would run into the millions of dollars.

components.note: 冖 here is a distorted form of 力 (strength) — a simplified way of showing soldiers grouped together.
车 (cart/vehicle) — 军 originally pictured soldiers riding out to battle in war chariots.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 他退伍后仍以曾是军人为荣。
example.pinyin: tā tuìwǔ hòu réng yǐ céng shì jūnrén wéi róng.
example.english: After discharge he was still proud to have been a soldier.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army, buried near Xi'an around 210 BC to guard China's first emperor in the afterlife, contains over 8,000 life-sized soldier statues. Each has individually sculpted facial features, and no two figures discovered so far are identical.

components.note: 冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'

example.hanzi: 公司即将迎来成立十周年。
example.pinyin: gōngsī jíjiāng yínglái chénglì shí zhōunián.
example.english: The company is about to celebrate its tenth anniversary.
example.fact: The Eiffel Tower was originally built as a temporary structure for the 1889 World's Fair, marking the 100th anniversary of the French Revolution. It was slated for demolition after 20 years but was saved because of its usefulness as a radio transmission tower.

components.note: 身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.
亻 (person) — the person receiving a share
分 (to divide) — the portion allotted to that person
讠 (speech) — the act of speaking.
正 (straight, correct) — speaking the straight, correct truth, giving 证 its meaning 'to prove, certify; evidence.'

example.hanzi: 办理业务需要出示身份证。
example.pinyin: bànlǐ yèwù xūyào chūshì shēnfènzhèng.
example.english: You need to show your ID card to handle this business.
example.fact: Estonia issues a mandatory national ID card that doubles as a digital signature key, letting citizens vote, file taxes, and sign legal contracts entirely online. Over 99% of Estonia's public services have been available digitally since the early 2000s.

components.note: 氵 (water) shows 沟 relates to a channel for water.
勾 (gōu) gives the exact sound of 沟.
辶 (to walk, movement) — 通 relates to passing through or getting somewhere.
甬 (yǒng) gives a hint of the sound — 通 is pronounced tōng, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 良好的沟通可以避免很多误会。
example.pinyin: liánghǎo de gōutōng kěyǐ bìmiǎn hěn duō wùhuì.
example.english: Good communication can avoid a lot of misunderstandings.
example.fact: Honeybees communicate the direction and distance of food sources through a "waggle dance," encoding the sun's position and flight distance in the angle and duration of their movements. It is a symbolic communication system unusually sophisticated for an insect.

components.note: 方 here depicts a flag or banner, marking a group on the move.
氏 depicts a person following behind — together, a group traveling together, giving 旅 its meaning 'trip, journey.'
氵 (water) — the sea or river being traveled through
斿 — a banner streaming in the wind, evoking free, drifting movement

example.hanzi: 暑假我们打算去云南旅游。
example.pinyin: shǔjià wǒmen dǎsuàn qù Yúnnán lǚyóu.
example.english: We plan to travel to Yunnan for summer vacation.
example.fact: Tourism now accounts for roughly 10% of global GDP and one in ten jobs worldwide. The industry ground to a near-total halt in 2020, when international arrivals fell by about 74%, the sharpest single-year drop ever recorded.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 政 relates to administering or governing.
正 (zhèng) gives the sound — 政 is also pronounced zhèng, an exact match.
⺮ (bamboo) — ancient policy documents were written on bamboo strips
朿 (cì) gives a sound distantly related to 策's reading cè, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 政府出台了新的环保政策。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ chūtái le xīn de huánbǎo zhèngcè.
example.english: The government introduced a new environmental policy.
example.fact: The 1987 Montreal Protocol, a global policy phasing out ozone-depleting chemicals, is considered one of the most successful environmental treaties ever. The ozone hole over Antarctica has been steadily shrinking since, and scientists project it could fully heal by around 2066.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
责 shows 贝 (money, a cowry shell) at its base, tied to a debt that must be repaid — giving 责 its meaning 'duty, responsibility, to blame.'

example.hanzi: 他因为迟到而受到老板的指责。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi chídào ér shòudào lǎobǎn de zhǐzé.
example.english: He was criticized by his boss for being late.
example.fact: Galileo was formally denounced and placed under house arrest by the Roman Inquisition in 1633 for supporting the idea that Earth orbits the Sun. The Catholic Church did not formally acknowledge his findings were correct until 1992.

components.note: Two lines curving apart from each other, originally meaning 'to divide, split' — the shape was later adopted to represent the number 'eight.'
卜 (divination) — 卦 (a divinatory diagram) belongs to fortune-telling.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to guà, sharing the initial consonant but having drifted apart in vowel over time.

example.hanzi: 同事们喜欢在午休时聊八卦。
example.pinyin: tóngshìmen xǐhuān zài wǔxiū shí liáo bāguà.
example.english: Coworkers like to chat about gossip during lunch break.
example.fact: Studies of primate behavior suggest gossip-like social grooming and information-sharing may have evolved as a way for early humans to track alliances and reputations in growing social groups. Some anthropologists argue this social function was itself a major driver behind the evolution of complex communication.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 汽 relates to water in its vapor form, steam.
气 (rising wisps) — depicts vapor drifting upward, together giving 汽 its meaning 'steam, gas.'
氵 (water) — 油 names an oily liquid.
由 (yóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 油.

example.hanzi: 车子的油箱里没有汽油了。
example.pinyin: chēzi de yóuxiāng lǐ méiyǒu qìyóu le.
example.english: There's no gasoline left in the car's tank.
example.fact: Gasoline is refined from crude oil through fractional distillation, which separates hydrocarbons by boiling point. A single barrel of crude oil yields only about 19 gallons of gasoline alongside diesel, jet fuel, and dozens of other refined products.

components.note: 口 (mouth), shown twice here, standing for eyes streaming with tears.
犬 (here a stand-in for a person, not literally 'dog') — a person crying, together giving 哭 its meaning 'to weep, to cry.'
氵 (water) — 泣 relates to tears.
立 (lì) gives a sound distantly related to qì, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 婴儿因为饿了而哭泣。
example.pinyin: yīng'ér yīnwèi è le ér kūqì.
example.english: The baby wept because it was hungry.
example.fact: Human emotional tears contain a different chemical composition than reflex tears caused by irritants like onions. They carry stress hormones and natural painkillers, leading some researchers to suggest crying may help the body regulate stress after intense emotion.

components.note: 贝 (shell) — ancient Chinese currency was made from cowrie shells, linking 贝 to wealth
才 (cái) gives the sound — an exact match with 财's reading cái
宀 (roof) — 富 relates to a well-stocked household, prosperous under its own roof
畐 (fú) gives a sound close to 富's reading fù, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 他把大部分财富都捐给了慈善机构。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ dà bùfèn cáifù dōu juān gěi le císhàn jīgòu.
example.english: He donated most of his wealth to charity.
example.fact: Economists estimate that the wealthiest 1% of the global population holds nearly half of all household wealth worldwide. That concentration has been rising steadily since the 1980s, according to long-running World Inequality Database research.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 没 originally meant to sink or drown in water, later extended to the negative 'not have.'
殳 (shū) is the historical sound component; it no longer rhymes with méi in modern Mandarin, another case of sound drift over time.
门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.

example.hanzi: 想让我借钱给你?没门!
example.pinyin: xiǎng ràng wǒ jiè qián gěi nǐ? méimén!
example.english: You want me to lend you money? No way!
example.fact: At the United Nations Security Council, any one of the five permanent members can single-handedly kill a resolution with a single "no" vote. That veto power has been exercised more than 300 times since 1946, more than half of them by the Soviet Union or Russia.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'

example.hanzi: 我们星期天一起去爬山吧。
example.pinyin: wǒmen xīngqītiān yìqǐ qù páshān ba.
example.english: Let's go hiking together on Sunday.
example.fact: The seven-day week has no basis in astronomy — it originated with the ancient Babylonians, who linked each day to one of the seven visible "wandering" celestial bodies known at the time. Those were the Sun, Moon, and the five planets visible to the naked eye.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 侄 names a family member, one's nephew.
至 (zhì) gives a sound close to zhí, the same syllable with a different tone.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 我的侄子今年上大学了。
example.pinyin: wǒ de zhízi jīnnián shàng dàxué le.
example.english: My nephew started college this year.
example.fact: Napoleon Bonaparte's nephew, Napoleon III, later became the first president of France and then its last monarch, ruling as emperor until 1870. They are one of history's few uncle-nephew pairs to each independently seize supreme power over the same country.

components.note: 泰 depicts a great volume of water 氺 being controlled or channeled from above — mastery over something so large came to suggest greatness, giving 泰 its meaning 'great, exalted.'
力 (strength) — 勒 relates to tightening or restraining with force.
革 (gé) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading lēi has diverged considerably.

example.hanzi: 泰勒是我们班新来的交换生。
example.pinyin: Tàilè shì wǒmen bān xīn lái de jiāohuàn shēng.
example.english: Taylor is the new exchange student in our class.
example.fact: The English surname Taylor derives from the medieval occupation of tailoring. It remains one of the most common English surnames precisely because clothing production was one of the largest trades in pre-industrial Europe, alongside names like Smith and Mason.

components.note: 良 is traditionally interpreted as a picture of a granary or storage structure with an opening for airflow, built to keep stored grain sound and unspoiled. Because a well-ventilated, well-built granary kept grain in good condition, the character came to mean 'good, fine, excellent' — the sense retained in 良心 'conscience.'
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 他的良心让他说出了实话。
example.pinyin: tā de liángxīn ràng tā shuō chū le shíhuà.
example.english: His conscience made him tell the truth.
example.fact: Phineas Gage, a 19th-century railway worker who survived a tamping iron piercing his skull in 1848, reportedly underwent a dramatic personality change afterward. The case became an early study that helped scientists link the brain's frontal lobe to moral judgment and impulse control.

components.note: 無-shaped top pictures a dancer holding decorated sleeves or fans.
舛 below pictures a pair of feet, together giving 舞 its meaning 'to dance.'
止 (a footprint), shown twice — one foot placed in front of the other, the source of 步's meaning 'step, pace.'

example.hanzi: 她练习了很多遍探戈的舞步。
example.pinyin: tā liànxí le hěn duō biàn tàngē de wǔbù.
example.english: She practiced the tango's dance steps many times over.
example.fact: Tango originated in the working-class port neighborhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the late 1800s, blending African, European, and South American musical traditions. It was initially considered scandalous and was banned from some European ballrooms when it first arrived around 1913.

components.note: 永 depicts a river with tributary streams branching off and flowing onward, an image of water extending into the distance without visible end. Because a river's course continues indefinitely, the character came to mean 'long, perpetual, forever' — the sense preserved in 永不 'never' (literally 'forever not').
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

example.hanzi: 她发誓永不放弃自己的梦想。
example.pinyin: tā fāshì yǒngbù fàngqì zìjǐ de mèngxiǎng.
example.english: She swore she would never give up on her dream.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is now over 15 billion miles from Earth and will likely keep drifting through interstellar space forever. Its power will run out around 2025, but the probe itself is destined to outlast our planet.

components.note: 宀 (roof/house) — 容's meaning 'to contain, hold' relates to a house holding things, extended to 'appearance, to allow, tolerate.'
刃 (blade) pictures something sharp and painful.
心 (heart) below suggests bearing pain in one's heart, giving 忍 its meaning 'to endure.'

example.hanzi: 老师容忍了学生的一些小错误。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī róngrěn le xuésheng de yìxiē xiǎo cuòwù.
example.english: The teacher tolerated some of the students' small mistakes.
example.fact: Coral reefs can tolerate only a narrow temperature range — a sustained rise of just 1-2°C above normal summer maximums triggers mass bleaching. This has occurred across large sections of Australia's Great Barrier Reef during repeated marine heatwaves since 2016.
